slides.title: OCP Contribution Process
slides.subtitle: Bring an idea through review to a useful public contribution.
slides.transcript: A contribution turns shared work into something others can use. For a specification, the path runs from an abstract through project and committee reviews to publication. Other contribution types have their own routes. Allow time for comments, revisions, and meetings; publication is not tied to a guaranteed date.

slides.transcript: The applicable agreement includes a thirty-day exclusion period. Waiving it is optional. An authorized representative from every contributing organization must notify the Foundation as required. A waiver changes the wait, not the need for committee approval. If you want the period to run, leave the optional waiver task incomplete. Confirm the choice with authorized people.

slides.title: Steps 15–16: confirm and publish
slides.transcript: Publication needs majority committee approval, your acknowledgement, and a completed exclusion period or valid waivers from every required organization. Read the decision. If you withdraw, tell Foundation staff in Chat before publication. This is the final confirmation. Once the conditions are met, Foundation staff publish the approved work in the Contribution Database and notify you. Check the listing and share its official link. A waiver never replaces the vote.

lms_catalog.title: OCP Contribution Process
lms_catalog.short_description: Follow an OCP specification from its first abstract through review, approval and publication.
lms_catalog.overview: A contribution turns useful work into a shared public resource. Follow the specification route through the Contribution Hub, understand who acts at each stage, and learn how clear documents and timely communication help the review progress.
lms_catalog.duration_note: Includes narration, videos, reading and the final two-question check. Optional close inspection of workflow screenshots and exploration of linked resources may take longer.

modules.summary: Choose the contribution type, prepare an abstract, review the Contributor License Agreement and use the correct template. Watch upload demonstrations and follow project and committee review, presentations and revisions. Understand the optional exclusion-period waiver, the approval and acknowledgement needed before publication, and how to communicate a withdrawal or share the published contribution.
